goal: Replace the loosely-typed AddArg/GetArg settings API with a compile-time typed Setting class, so setting names, types, and default values are checked by the compiler instead of relying on convention.
Aims to eliminate a recurring class of bugs where the same setting is registered and retrieved with inconsistent types or default values across the codebase.

A reviewer's open correctness question from 2026-08-20 about silent behavior changes (dropped null array elements, untracked GetArg<T> template calls) has no visible author reply yet.
agreement: Concept ACKs from l0rinc, hodlinator, and jeanpablojp with no outright objections to the goal.

jeanpablojp raised an unresolved but nonblocking concern that the 'pure refactor' claim may not hold: some settings silently change behavior (dropped null list elements, a naming collision bug between ProxySetting and ProxySettingStr) (jeanpablojp).
Reviewers (hodlinator, l0rinc, maflcko) have pushed many design nits over a year, most incorporated by the author, with a few open threads on API design left unresolved (hodlinator).

Leverage is high: the author states this is a prerequisite for a runtime-validation follow-up (#22978) and for cleaner interfaces than the ALLOW_* flag system (#16545).

result.summary: This PR introduces a common::Setting template that lets settings be declared once with a name, C++ type, help text, and default, replacing the current pattern of separate AddArg() registration and untyped GetArg()/GetBoolArg()/GetPathArg() retrieval calls scattered across the codebase. A large scripted-diff commit then mechanically replaces essentially every AddArg/GetArg call site (100 files, +3713/-1113) with the new typed Register()/Get() calls generated by a temporary Python script. The author states the change is a pure refactor with no intended behavior change, laying groundwork for future runtime setting validation (tracked in #22978).
result.problem: The current settings API lets setting names be misspelled, retrieval types diverge from registration types, and default values be duplicated inconsistently between help text and retrieval sites; this has caused real bugs (cited: #30529, #31212) and makes it hard to add validation. Developers touching settings code feel this most, since nothing catches these mismatches until runtime or a bug report.

open_concerns: jeanpablojp (2026-08-20): the scripted-diff silently changes behavior in edge cases — a null element in a settings.json list array is now dropped instead of throwing, and the ProxySetting/ProxySettingStr naming split creates a footgun where changing one string breaks the other silently; no visible author response.

jeanpablojp (2026-08-20): the script's regex misses templated GetArg<T>() calls (five settings including -prevoutfetchthreads, -rpcworkqueue, -blockmaxweight), leaving them outside the typed migration; not obviously resolved.

hodlinator (2026-08-26, 2026-09-14): several design questions remain open, e.g. whether to remove now-unused SettingTraits overloads and GetPtr(), and how to better document the 'legacy' option flag; author has not replied to the latest round.
resolved_concerns: Early template syntax and code-clarity nits (StringLiteral deduction guide, auto parameter types, missing typename) raised by hodlinator and l0rinc were fixed by the author.
maflcko's suggestion to convert manual default-value handling into DefaultFn for a couple of wallet settings was implemented in a later push.
Camel-casing dictionary suggestion for setting names was accepted and implemented.
Compile-time overhead question was investigated by hodlinator and found negligible.

result.card: This PR replaces Bitcoin Core's untyped AddArg()/GetArg() settings API with a compile-time typed common::Setting template, and mechanically rewrites essentially every settings call site in the codebase (100 files, +3713/-1113) to use it via a temporary code-generation script. The problem it targets is real: mismatched setting names, types, and duplicated default values in the old API have caused actual bugs, cited by the author as fixed in #30529 and #31212, and the change is described as a stepping stone toward runtime setting validation tracked in issue #22978. Review has been active for over a year with three concept ACKs (l0rinc, hodlinator, jeanpablojp) and no concept objections, but reviewer jeanpablojp found concrete cases where the 'pure refactor, no behavior change' claim doesn't fully hold (a silently dropped null list element, a ProxySetting/ProxySettingStr naming footgun), left unresolved. The PR carries a Needs rebase label with a dirty merge state and has required 49 force-pushes against dozens of conflicting open PRs, making it Stale for review purposes even though the underlying goal is well received. Only the utils, tests, and build categories are substantively affected; every other touched area (wallet, rpc, validation, mempool, mining, p2p, indexes, ipc, kernel, tools) sees only mechanical call-site rewrites with no behavior change to that area's logic.
